# Commentary on Wage Labour and Capital (WLC)

Generated from `commentary/` and `renderings/`. Each tradition writes in its own files; see docs/commentary-guide.md.

## WLC · Engels revised the whole text in 1891 so that workers sell labour-power, not labour

**General (no particular tradition)** · Later theory (revises) · status: proposed · `general:engels-labour-to-labour-power`

Engels explains that his changes all turn on one point: in the original the worker sells his labour to the
capitalist, in the revised text his labour-power (WLC P1891.5.1, WLC P1891.5.2). He made the change because Marx
worked out the distinction only later, in the 1850s, and in Capital. Each change is recorded as an 1849 variant
on its verse, for example WLC I.13.1.

By: WLC P1891.5.1; WLC P1891.5.2

Sources:
- Engels, Introduction to Wage Labour and Capital (1891), MEW 22, pp. 202-209

See also: WLC I.13.1, WLC IV.9.1

## WLC I.4.1 · Marx announced three parts; only the first was published

**General (no particular tradition)** · Background · status: proposed · `general:unfinished-plan`

Marx promised to treat the relation of wage labour to capital, the ruin of the middle classes, and the
commercial subjugation of the bourgeois classes of the other European nations by England (WLC I.4.1). The
series broke off after the fifth instalment. Engels gives the reason: the Russian invasion of Hungary and the
uprisings of spring 1849, which led to the paper itself being shut down on 19 May 1849 (WLC P1891.1.3).

Sources:
- Engels, Introduction to Wage Labour and Capital (1891)
